published_finding: yield change per +1 C: maize -7.4, wheat -6.0, rice -3.2, soybean -3.1 (n.s.) -> maize > wheat > rice > soybean
our_comparable_result: climate part E x S (equal weights): maize > wheat > soybean > rice; Spearman rho with Zhao = +0.8 (n = 4)
interpretation: Our climate part (E x S, no importance) orders maize above wheat as Zhao does; rice and soybean swap (Zhao's soybean estimate is not significant). Importance, not climate, moves wheat above maize in the full index. n = 4: descriptive only.

published_finding: wheat loss per +1 C: India -9.1, Russia -7.8, USA -5.5, China -2.6 %
our_comparable_result: wheat heat exposure E_heat: India 0.115, Russia 0.015, USA 0.015, China 0.002
interpretation: India has the highest wheat heat exposure in both; Russia's high index score comes from water deficit, a channel Zhao's temperature regression does not isolate.

published_finding: Russia wheat production about -15 % from temperature trends
our_comparable_result: wheat-Russia F4 = 0.1315 (top pair); heat part 0.0027 vs water part 0.1288
interpretation: Both flag Russian wheat; Lobell attributes it to temperature, our monthly-threshold measure attributes it mostly to rainfed water deficit (heat above 25 C T_eff is rare in monthly means).

paper: Ray et al. 2015 Nat. Commun.; Ray et al. 2019 PLoS ONE
crop: rice vs other cereals and soybean
published_finding: climate explains 32-39 % of yield variability; rice least
our_comparable_result: rice climate part E x S = 0.0247, lowest of the four (wheat 0.1077, maize 0.1345, soybean 0.0830)
interpretation: Ray et al. measure the share of observed yield VARIABILITY that climate explains, not vulnerability. Low explained variability is not evidence of low vulnerability (irrigation can buffer variability, and damage that monthly data cannot see is not in either measure). Our rice climate part is lowest of the four, in line with their ordering, but the earlier reading as independent support for a low rice score is withdrawn (18-19 Nov 2026 audit).

scenario: RCP8.5 without CO2 (RCP4.5 with CO2 in brackets)
our_comparable_result: our conditional yield change (mean over countries, no CO2): maize -2.5 %, wheat -3.5 %, soybean +0.7 %
agreement: sign agrees for maize; sign agrees for wheat; sign differs for soybean; our magnitudes smaller
interpretation: Ours counts only heat above thresholds and rainfed deficit at monthly resolution under SSP2-4.5, so smaller losses are expected; with CO2 fertilisation C3 wheat and soybean gain in Deryng, which our index excludes.

paper: Challinor et al. 2014 Nat. Clim. Change
our_comparable_result: 76 % of our 59 pairs show a climate-driven yield loss (literature accounting); cereals only: 74 %
interpretation: Our losses come only from heat above crop thresholds and rainfed deficit; pairs below the heat threshold and getting wetter show gains.

published_finding: suitable area: Africa -7 to -11 %, South America -5 %, India marginal areas become unsuitable
our_comparable_result: maize change in F4 2041-60 vs 1971-2000: South Africa -0.0127, Brazil +0.0019, India -0.0002
interpretation: Our maize scores fall in South Africa because MRI-ESM2-0 gives a smaller rainfed deficit there; suitability models use annual climate envelopes and more extreme scenarios. Single-GCM result.

paper: Rippke et al. 2016 Nat. Clim. Change; Hummel et al. 2018 Sci. Rep.
published_finding: beans ~10 % area needing transformation in Uganda/Tanzania by the 2050s (RP); most SE African bean areas unsuitable by 2040-69, drought-driven (HU)
our_comparable_result: bean-Tanzania F4 change +0.0188; conditional yield change -17.7 %
interpretation: Beans are among the crops whose vulnerability rises most in our results too; ours is driven by heat above the bean threshold.

published_finding: -0.8 to -5.7 % production at +2 C with CO2 fixed (+3 to +11 % with CO2)
our_comparable_result: rapeseed-Canada conditional yield change -3.2 % (no CO2); flowering T_eff change +3.1 C
interpretation: Same sign when CO2 fertilisation is excluded.

published_finding: yields fall with warmer seasons: chickpea -0.53 to -3.01, mustard -0.92 to -2.01 q/ha per C
our_comparable_result: India 2041-60: chickpea T_eff +1.3 C, yield -0.2 %; rapeseed-mustard T_eff +1.6 C, yield -2.2 %
interpretation: Direction consistent; Kalra is a seasonal-mean regression, ours a flowering-threshold measure.
